In [[differential geometry]], the '''Kirwan map''', introduced by British mathematician [[Frances Kirwan]], is the [[homomorphism]]
:<math>H^*_G(M) \to H^*(M /\!/_p G)</math>
where
*<math>M</math> is a [[Hamiltonian group action|Hamiltonian G-space]]; i.e., a [[symplectic manifold]] acted by a Lie group ''G'' with a [[moment map]] <math>\mu: M \to {\mathfrak g}^*</math>.
*<math>H^*_G(M)</math> is the [[equivariant cohomology ring]] of <math>M</math>; i.e.. the cohomology ring of the [[homotopy quotient]] <math>EG \times_G M</math> of <math>M</math> by <math>G</math>.
*<math>M /\!/_p G = \mu^{-1}(p)/G</math> is the [[symplectic quotient]] of <math>M</math> by <math>G</math> at a regular central value <math> p \in Z({\mathfrak g}^*) </math> of <math>\mu</math>.

It is defined as the map of equivariant cohomology induced by the inclusion <math>\mu^{-1}(p) \hookrightarrow M</math> followed by the canonical isomorphism <math>H_G^*(\mu^{-1}(p)) = H^*(M /\!/_p G)</math>.

A theorem of Kirwan<ref>{{cite book |author1-link=Frances Kirwan |first=F.C. |last=Kirwan |title=Cohomology of Quotients in Complex and Algebraic Geometry |series=Mathematical Notes |volume=31 |publisher=Princeton University Press |date=1984 |isbn=978-0-691-21456-6 |url={{GBurl|4wfZBnlSaJ0C|pg=PP5}}}}</ref> says that if <math>M</math> is [[Compact space|compact]], then the map is surjective in rational coefficients. The analogous result holds between the [[K-theory]] of the symplectic quotient and the equivariant topological K-theory of <math>M</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Harada |first2=G. |last2=Landweber |title=Surjectivity for Hamiltonian G-spaces in K-theory |journal=Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. |volume=359 |date=2007 |issue=12 |pages=6001–25 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-07-04164-5 |jstor=20161853 |arxiv=math/0503609 |s2cid=17690407 |url=https://www.ams.org/tran/2007-359-12/S0002-9947-07-04164-5/}}</ref>
